name: m4-leyden-l2-fix
description: L2 of the Leyden evaluation rerun with the compiler fix that keeps `scala.reflect.runtime` out of the AOT cache (retronym/scala#250: no `TypeTag` in the `f` interpolator, so `JavaMirror` is never loaded and the cache never links `SynchronizedSymbol`).

In `m4-leyden-l2-scala` (build 1e85ab8eba) cached forks ran +2.9–3.7% slower than cold with +8% instructions, because `SynchronizedSymbol`'s overrides of `Symbol.getFlag`/`validTo` stopped C2 inlining them by CHA. Question: with the fix, do cached forks match cold at steady state?

Build: branch `claude/perf-integration-no-typetag` (scala2-perf-integration, which includes retronym/scala#249, plus #250's two commits), stock JDK 26 integration build, m4. Arms as in `m4-leyden-l2-scala`.

variantDescriptions.aot: one cache, trained by a fork with the same JMH arguments (`-wi 8 -i 5`)
variantDescriptions.aot-short: one cache, trained by a 3-iteration fork (`-wi 2 -i 1`)
